name: Alpenzoo Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: Europe's highest themed zoo on the southern slopes of Nordkette above Innsbruck is home to some 2,000 alpine animals in natural habitats.
preis: Adults approx. €14.00; reduced tickets for children; combination tickets with Hungerburgbahn available
oeffnungszeiten: Open 365 days a year daily 09:00 to 18:00 (winter months until 17:00)
beschreibung:
Overview

World-famous Alpenzoo Innsbruck-Tirol nestles against the sunny southern slopes of the striking Nordkette high above the rooftops of Tyrol's regional capital at 750 meters above sea level. As Europe's highest themed zoo, it is devoted entirely to the wildlife of the alpine region. Across spacious hillside grounds designed close to nature, around 2,000 fascinating alpine animals representing 150 species reside, including brown bears, elusive wolves, lynx, ibex, chamois, playful river otters, and rare bearded vultures. Founded in 1962 by passionate zoologist Hans Psenner, the zoo has earned international recognition for pioneering breeding and reintroduction programs for endangered alpine wildlife. Another standout highlight is the world's largest cold-water alpine aquarium, providing fascinating glimpses into the aquatic life of mountain streams and lakes.

Route & Requirements

The zoo path climbs via winding paths and paved terraces through steep woodland terrain, covering about 100 meters of elevation. Visitors should plan about two to three hours for a complete tour. All main paths are paved, though some sections have steep gradients due to the hillside topography; visitors pushing sturdy strollers or using manual wheelchairs can navigate the grounds well (electric wheelchair pulling devices can be rented at the ticket desk). Sturdy, comfortable walking shoes are advisable. Shaded resting benches and viewpoints along the route offer scenic pauses with panoramic vistas over Innsbruck. Children enjoy the show farm with rare domestic breeds, petting areas, and multiple adventure playgrounds with bear slides and climbing walls. Accessible restrooms and dining options are available for families.

Visit & Arrival

Alpenzoo is open 365 days a year: daily 09:00 to 18:00 in summer, and 09:00 to 17:00 during winter. The most spectacular way to arrive is from Innsbruck city center via the futuristic Hungerburgbahn funicular (Station Alpenzoo, followed by a five-minute walk). By bus, IVB line W travels directly from Marktplatz to the zoo entrance. Motorists access the zoo via Weiherburggasse (pay parking is available, but fills quickly at peak hours).

Tips

Purchase the discounted Nordkettenbahnen combination ticket, which includes the Hungerburgbahn ride and zoo admission. Be sure not to miss the daily commented feedings of the otters and wolves, hosted by experienced zookeepers.
